Three developers built different entry points, each handling Unicode usernames their own way. The service appeared to work during initial testing with ASCII usernames, but once users with accented names signed up, reports started coming in: some users can't log in, deposits vanish into the wrong account, the CLI can't find accounts that exist in the web interface, and the monthly export CSV shows what look like duplicate usernames with different balances. The existing database already contains several accounts in mixed Unicode forms, including duplicate entries for the same visual username.",
  "environment_setup": "The Dockerfile installs Flask, Click, and other dependencies, then copies a ~1500-line Python project into /app/account_service/. An init_db.py script runs at build time to populate /app/data/accounts.db with a mix of accounts: some stored in NFC form (imported), some in NFD form (registered via the API), and one visual username ('café') existing as two separate accounts (NFC with balance 500, NFD with balance 300). The init script is deleted after build. The codebase includes: config.py (sets NORMALIZATION_FORM='NFD'), normalize.py (normalize_for_storage reads config, normalize_for_display hardcodes NFC), validation.py (sanitize_username strips+lowercases but never normalizes — decoy), middleware.py (normalizes URL paths to NFC — decoy), routes/auth.py (register skips normalization, login calls normalize_for_storage), routes/accounts.py (balance ops call normalize_for_storage), routes/admin.py (adjust_balance takes raw username with no normalization at all), cli.py (create skips normalization, lookup hardcodes unicodedata.normalize('NFC') directly), import_export.py (import hardcodes NFC directly, export dumps raw usernames). The balance_history table also stores raw usernames, creating additional data inconsistency.",
  "instruction_summary": "The account service at /app/account_service/ has several interrelated problems. Users with accented characters in their usernames experience login failures, missing deposits, and CLI lookup failures. The account export CSV shows what appear to be duplicate usernames. Your job is to fix the service so that: (1) Every visually identical username is treated as the same account regardless of Unicode encoding form — two usernames that look identical on screen must always resolve to one account. (2) All entry points (web API routes, CLI commands, import/export) handle usernames consistently. (3) The account export at /app/data/export.csv must contain no visually duplicate usernames when generated by `python3 -m account_service.cli export /app/data/export.csv`. (4) Existing duplicate accounts in /app/data/accounts.db must be merged — balances combined into a single canonical account per visual username, with the NFC form as canonical. (5) The balance_history table must be updated to reflect merged accounts. (6) After your fixes, the web service must start on port 5000 and the CLI must work.   "solution_outline": [

    "In routes/admin.py, add sanitize_username() and normalize_for_storage() calls in adjust_balance() before lookups",
